card.name: Dosing and preparation instructions wording
card.fires_on: The last piece of a drug name, a dose unit, or a preparation term inside instructions for diluting, infusing or giving a product. It fires on words such as hydrochloride, premixed, water for injection, infusion set, and mg after a strength.

modes.label: Drug or product name endings
modes.description: Final part of a drug or product name or a preparation term in mixing and infusion steps.
modes.example: aseptically transfer the appropriate quantity (see chart) of diltiazem hydrochlor<<ide>> injection to the desired volume of either Normal

modes.label: Units after strengths
modes.description: mg or % right after a number in a tablet strength or solution concentration.
modes.example: Ledipasvir and Sofosbuvir (HARVONI) 45<< mg>>/200 mg tablet once daily

modes.label: Preparation equipment and diluents
modes.description: Words naming diluent or equipment in preparation steps, such as water for injection or an infusion set.
modes.example: DO NOT USE BACTERIOSTATIC<< WATER>> FOR INJECTION CONTAINING BENZ

card.writes: It seems to push toward words like available and popular, but the effect is weak and unclear.
